concept: Breadcrumb prints the path to this page the way a device prints its menu trail on the case: names in a row, joined by a short run of dots, with the page you are on carrying one ink index mark. On a narrow unit the middle names fold into one key that prints them back when pressed.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a breadcrumb of grey links split by a greater-than sign or a slash, the last name in bold
default_to_avoid.why_not: The separator is a typed character that a screen reader may read out, and the current page is told by weight alone, which is the default every web breadcrumb has.

default_to_avoid.pattern: a row of pills or tags, one per level, the last filled with the accent colour
default_to_avoid.why_not: Pills read as keys that set a filter, and an accent fill spends the unit's one orange on a path.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): band names printed in a row on the case, the scale joined by printed marks
system/FORM.md display class: text is flat printing on the material, no height, no shadow
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Breadcrumb pattern: a nav landmark, an ordered list, aria-current=page on the last item

derivation.consequence: the chosen word carries one ink index mark beside it
derivation.form: The current page is plain text, not a link, and carries the same short ink index mark as the chosen name in Tabs, so it is told by a shape and not by weight alone.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The first name starts at the inset line of the unit and the row never leaves it: names, leaders and the folded key share one baseline.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Each link and the folded key are 44px tall and at least the touch width, though the printed name is small.

derivation.consequence: hover only darkens a key's ink a step
derivation.form: A link darkens one ink step on hover and nothing else moves, because printing on a case does not rise.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Links, leaders, the index mark and the folded key are all ink, never orange.

options.name: dotted leader with an index mark under the current page

variants.reason: C reuses the dotted rail of Stepper and the index mark of Tabs, so the path looks printed on the same case; A and B are the slash and the chevron every web breadcrumb already has, and both tell the current page by weight alone.

root.why: A nav landmark with a name, so assistive tech lists it among the page's regions and the path sits on one inset line.

list.why: An ordered list in one row that never wraps while folded, so the path keeps one baseline and its length can be measured.

item.why: One level of the path, 44px tall so a link or the folded key inside it keeps the full hit area.

link.why: An ancestor is a real link printed in secondary ink in the label size, a plain anchor so the browser keeps its own open and copy behaviour.

current.why: The page you are on is text in primary ink and medium weight, announced with aria-current=page, and it is not a link to itself.

mark.why: One short ink bar under the current name, the same shape Tabs uses for its chosen name, so the current page is told by a mark you can see in grey.

leader.why: A short run of printed dots between two names, the way Stepper joins its windows; it is hidden from assistive tech because the list already carries the order.

more.why: The folded middle names are one key with three dots. It announces that it is collapsed, and pressing it prints every name back in the row.

hover.why: Hover darkens a link one ink step and nothing rises, because printing on a case does not move.

focus-visible.why: Keyboard focus draws the same dark ring around a link or the folded key as on every part of the system.

data-collapsed.why: When the full path does not fit the unit's width, the middle names fold into the folded key, so the row stays on one line and nothing reflows between states.

data-hidden.why: A middle name is only taken out of the row while the path is folded; it stays in the document order once the key prints it back.

data-more.why: The level that holds the folded key exists only while the path is folded, and it is the one place a key stands in a row of names.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion nothing on the row moves, and the hover ink step keeps its short fade because a fade of colour moves nothing.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the leader dots and the index mark draw in the system text colour, so the path and the current page keep their marks.

data-open.why: Once the folded key has been pressed, or when folding is turned off, the row may wrap onto more lines so every name stays visible instead of hiding again.

color.why: The ink step on hover comes in over 120ms and goes back over 240ms on the decelerating curve (motion.hover with kiln.state), fast in and slow out; only the colour changes and no part travels.
